title: Recomposition Is Not The Enemy
excerpt: I spent a weekend trying to eliminate recomposition entirely before realizing that was never the goal — unnecessary recomposition was.
bodyMarkdown:
Somewhere along the way I absorbed the idea that recomposition is expensive and should be avoided like a layout pass in the old View system. It isn't, and treating it that way led me to write worse code, not better code. > Recomposition should be fast enough that you don't think about it. The job is to make it cheap, not to make it rare. Compose recomposes functions, not the whole tree, and it skips work for composables whose inputs haven't changed. The actual problem I was hitting wasn't recomposition itself — it was *unstable* parameters causing recomposition to skip nothing at all. ## The `Stable` and `Immutable` story A class Compose can't prove is stable forces every composable that reads it to recompose on every pass, whether or not anything actually changed. Two fixes worked for me: 1. Prefer `data class` with `val` properties and immutable collections (`ImmutableList` from `kotlinx.collections.immutable`, not a raw `List` backed by a mutable `ArrayList`). 2. Mark genuinely-stable classes explicitly with `@Stable` or `@Immutable` when Compose's own inference can't see far enough — usually because the class lives in a module Compose's compiler plugin isn't looking at. ## Measuring instead of guessing Layout Inspector's recomposition counts turned this from folklore into something I could actually check. I added a debug border via `Modifier.background` toggling on a `remember` flag tied to a recomposition counter, and watched which rows in a `LazyColumn` were repainting on every scroll frame for no reason. Turned out to be a lambda allocated fresh on every parent recomposition, breaking `equals` comparison for the child's `onClick` parameter — swapping it for a remembered lambda fixed it immediately. The lesson that stuck: don't reach for `remember`, `derivedStateOf`, or manual skipping as a first move. Reach for them once you've actually measured a hot path, because the default behavior is already good. ## Quick checklist before you optimize - Confirm the recomposition is actually happening more than expected using Layout Inspector, not a hunch. - Check whether the parameter causing it is a lambda, a mutable collection, or a class Compose can't infer as stable. - Only then reach for `remember`, `@Stable`, or an immutable collection type.
Read the official Compose performance guide
For the deeper mechanics, the [Jetpack Compose phases documentation](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/compose/phases) walks through composition, layout, and drawing as three distinct, independently-skippable stages.

Sources:
